features.name: Capabilities: named, but never declared
features.pitch: Write the functions and the type conforms. No impl blocks, and no two modules can give one type two meanings.
features.detail: A capability is a named set of operations, and a type conforms as soon as its defs supply every one. The compiler infers the conformance, so there is no `impl` boilerplate for a model to forget or get wrong. Coherence is fixed by law: a (type, capability) pair has exactly one origin in the whole program, a second `extend` is a compile error, and a conformance the checker cannot decide within entailment depth 12 is rejected, never accepted. So whether code compiles never depends on import order, and an agent's edit cannot quietly change which implementation a call reaches.
features.status_evidence: draconyx-types: solve.rs does structural matching, conditional conformance by entailment chaining with ENTAILMENT_DEPTH = 12, and the occurs guard. lib.rs codes AX0420 missing conformance, AX0421 bound not satisfied, AX0422 two origins, AX0423 asserts without conformance, AX0424 not object-safe, AX0425 undecided. Covered by tests/reject cond_conformance_*, asserts_without_conformance*. One gap: per-ownership conformance (`share T : C` as a separate judgement, plus the `when transfer/share/remote` arms) is listed under 'Not implemented' in draconyx-types/src/lib.rs, so leave it out of this claim.
features.sample:
capability Add:
    def add(transfer self: Self, transfer other: Self) -> Self

struct Tensor:
    data: List<Float>

def add(transfer self: Tensor, transfer other: Tensor) -> Tensor

features.name: Algebraic laws as code, checked at build time
features.pitch: In C++ and Rust, associativity is a line in the docs. In Draconyx it is a `law` line, and a false one fails the build with a shrunk counter-example.
features.detail: A capability can carry laws such as associative, identity or commutative. A type has to assert them explicitly, because laws are never inferred from names. A `checked` law, the default mode, becomes a property test: inputs come from Arbitrary, the first failure is shrunk, and the witness is saved to a regression file that later runs replay first. The `proven` mode (SMT or proof term) is specified but not built, so today the guarantee is property-tested, not proved.
features.status_evidence: Built: draconyx-eval/src/harness.rs and arbitrary.rs run `drx test` / `drx verify` (draconyx-cli main.rs). That covers checked laws as property tests with greedy shrinking and replayed regression files, conditional laws with a vacuity guard, in-expectation laws and witness examples, reported as AX0701 law violation and AX0704 vacuous law. Not built: the `proven` mode. harness.rs says a proven law is 'not discharged: no solver in v0', and draconyx-types lib.rs lists 'law verification itself... nothing is tested or proved' only for the typechecker crate. There is no SMT backend anywhere.
features.sample:
capability Monoid:
    def add(transfer self: Self, transfer other: Self) -> Self
    def zero() -> Self
    law associative: add(self = add(self = a, other = b), other = c)
                     == add(self = a, other = add(self = b, other = c))
    law identity:    add(self = a, other = zero()) == a

features.name: Dispatch on algebra
features.pitch: Write the parallel reduction once. The compiler picks it only for types that assert the laws that make it correct.
features.detail: A generic def can branch on which laws its type argument asserts, not just on which capability it has. The arms are tried in order from most demanding to least, and the checker enforces totality and flags redundant arms. A model can write the fast path and the safe fallback side by side, and the type system decides which one is legal for each type. Arms are chosen on asserted laws, and the law harness is what checks those assertions.
features.status_evidence: draconyx-types checks law-qualified bounds (decision 19, `over_same_ops`), plus `when` totality and redundancy in the AX06xx band (tests/reject when_total, when_non_total, when_redundant, when_unreachable). At run time, draconyx-eval interp.rs `Machine::holds` picks the arm, and the native image reaches it through draconyx-runtime (index.rs WhenArm, `ax_when_arm`). Decision 236 memoizes the arm under the full question, pinned by units3/c36-when-cap-args.
features.sample:
def reduce<T>(xs: List<T>) -> T where T : Add
    when T : Add associative + commutative -> parallel_tree_reduce(xs)
    when T : Add associative                -> sequential_left_fold(xs)
    when T : Add commutative                -> unordered_fold(xs)
    when T : Add                            -> sequential_left_fold(xs)

features.name: Generics that infer the hard parts
features.pitch: Variance, associated types and const-generic shapes are worked out by the compiler, not annotated by the model.
features.detail: Generics use angle brackets. Variance is inferred from field positions, so there are no +T/-T annotations. Associated types are solved from the conformer's defs, `some C`/`any C` existentials give opaque results and heterogeneous, dynamically dispatched collections, and const generics make `Vec<Float, 3>` and `Vec<Float, 4>` different types. Dimension equality (`N + M` is `M + N`) and literal bounds (`head` of a `Vec<T, 0>`) are checked in every build. Refinement types such as `{ x: Int | x > 0 }` are only partly built: the checker discharges literals and facts from `if` guards, and the SMT discharge the spec calls for, also needed for symbolic value-parameter bounds, does not exist yet.
features.status_evidence: Built in draconyx-types: variance.rs (decision 24, field positions to a fixpoint), associated types and object safety (decision 22, tests/reject assoc_equality*), existential subsumption (exist_subsumption / exist_no_subsumption), with `Ty::Exist` evaluated in draconyx-eval interp.rs. Const generics are equal by normalization, literal bounds give AX1021 (decision 29, tests const_generics_ok, const_mismatch, const_bound_violated). Partial: refinements are 'refinement-lite' in pred.rs, with syntactic discharge only from literals and if-guard facts and the purity rule AX1018. An undischarged predicate or a symbolic value-parameter bound is only a note (AX1009 REFINEMENT_NOT_CHECKED). lib.rs lists 'symbolic value-parameter entailment' under Not implemented, and there is no SMT backend.
features.sample:
struct Vec<T, const N: Int>:
    data: Array<T>            // a vector of exactly N elements

def dot<T, const N: Int>(a: Vec<T, N>, b: Vec<T, N>) -> T
    where T : Ring

features.name: Ownership spelled at both ends
features.pitch: Every handover is written where the value is given and again where it is taken, so a model never has to guess who owns what.
features.detail: Four authorities: owned (consumed with `transfer`), `borrow` (exclusive), readonly borrow (the unmarked default), and `share`/`observe` for co-owning and non-owning handles. The spec's words are owned/borrow/share/observe, not Owned/Borrow/Shared/Weak. The verb is part of the published signature and must be repeated at the call site (the mirror principle), so a mismatch is a compile error that names both halves instead of a silent aliasing bug. Generated code shows its data flow in the text an agent reads, with no inference needed.
features.status_evidence: compiler/crates/draconyx-own (check.rs, model.rs) checks each argument's verb against the parameter or field verb at every call and construction site, function types included. It runs on `drx check` (draconyx-cli/src/main.rs:476), on `drx run`/`drx build` through draconyx-eval/src/load.rs:255, and in the daemon. An implicit deep copy of a heap value is AX0321.
features.sample:
start_engine(vehicle: Vehicle)             // readonly borrow: the default
tune(borrow engine: Engine)                // exclusive, mutable borrow
mount_wheels(transfer car: Vehicle,
             transfer wheel1: Wheel, ...)  // consumed: spelled at both ends

features.name: Borrow checking with zero lifetime syntax
features.pitch: Rust-grade memory safety without a single `'a`: you never write a lifetime, and the compiler works out every one.
features.detail: A borrow lasts until its last use (non-lexical lifetimes), not until the end of its scope. The law of exclusivity holds: one exclusive borrow or any number of readonly ones at a time. Owned values are linear, so a use after move is a compile error. The spec has no lifetime parameters at all, which removes the annotation puzzles that models most often get wrong in Rust, while still rejecting dangling borrows, use-after-free and aliased mutation.
features.status_evidence: draconyx-own enforces linearity (AX0312 use-after-move, AX0303 move out of a borrow), exclusivity through field paths, and NLL liveness (live.rs). The checker calls itself 'NLL-lite': liveness follows structured control flow, and break/continue/return are treated conservatively, so it can reject code the spec accepts but never accepts unsafe code. The spec allows exactly this ('incomplete rather than incorrect', sections/07:75-82).

features.name: Views inferred, not annotated
features.pitch: Put a borrow in a struct and it becomes a safe view on its own: no keyword, no lifetime parameter.
features.detail: A struct or enum with a `borrow` field or payload, directly or through generics, is a view struct. The checker treats the whole value as one borrow of what it points into. View-ness is worked out from the structure, so `Option<borrow T>` and slice-like windows need no annotation. The checker also refuses to let a view escape a function unless every borrow it holds comes from a parameter.
features.status_evidence: draconyx-own/src/lib.rs (views): a value whose type carries a borrow inherits the borrows it was built from. A borrow or view may leave a def only when it derives from a parameter (AX0305), and a view type may not define `drop` (AX0309). Closure capture modes are inferred the same way.
features.sample:
struct Slice<T>:
    data:  borrow List<T>   // a borrow field -> Slice is a VIEW
    start: Int
    end:   Int

features.name: No garbage collector, deterministic drops
features.pitch: No tracing GC and no pauses: each value is freed the moment its last owner lets go.
features.detail: The spec fixes what each authority compiles to. Owned values and borrows carry no runtime bookkeeping. `share` uses precise reference counting inserted by the compiler (Perceus-style), reuses memory in place when a value has a single owner, and makes counts atomic only when analysis shows a value crosses threads. `observe` is a generational reference checked at `upgrade`. Today's runtime already gives deterministic, pause-free freeing and drop order; the zero-cost and Perceus parts of that design are not built yet.
features.status_evidence: Built: draconyx-runtime (val.rs) and draconyx-eval keep every heap value in a Rust `Rc`, and `observe` is an `Rc` weak handle (interp.rs:1376, `upgrade` in intrinsics.rs:493). `drop` witnesses run when the last owner dies (interp.rs drop_value/sole_owner). There is no tracing collector anywhere. Not built: owned values are refcounted too instead of having zero bookkeeping, and there is no Perceus dup/drop placement or reuse analysis, no analysis that selects atomic counts, and no generational references. Cycles of `share` leak, as the spec states.
features.sample:
let cache: share Cache = share empty()       // refcount = 1

let worker = share cache                     // compiler inserts dup -> count = 2
spawn(() -> process(worker))                // worker handed off

features.name: Remote values that cannot hide failure
features.pitch: In Draconyx a network call never looks like a local call: `remote` is in the type, and every way it can fail is a value you have to match on.
features.detail: `remote T` is a type qualifier, and the standard `RemoteError` sum gives four reasons for failure: Unreachable, Timeout, Partitioned and NodeGone. Code generated by a model therefore has to say what happens on a slow link and what happens on a dead node. It cannot be written as if the network were always up. Sharing (`share`) and observing (`observe`) a remote value are compile errors because they would need distributed refcounting, which cannot be made correct.
features.status_evidence: The checker handles this part. draconyx-types carries `remote` as a qualifier (ty.rs:90). A send to a remote actor handle is typed `Result<Unit, RemoteError>` (expr.rs:1320). An `isolated` extern call is typed `Result<T, RemoteError>` (call.rs:1086). draconyx-own rejects `share remote` and `observe remote` with AX0308 (check.rs:305-318, tested in own.rs:638-650). The std prelude declares `RemoteError` with all four variants (draconyx-corpus/src/stdlib.rs:195). Nothing runs remotely: the interpreter never takes a `remote` arm (interp.rs:2513), and the native backend refuses remote forms with AX1105 (codegen emit.rs:442,485). The rule that every remote operation is fallible is enforced only for sends and isolated externs, not in general.
features.sample:
def read_temperature(sensor: remote Sensor) -> Result<Float>

match read_temperature(sensor):
    Ok(celsius)        -> record(celsius)
    Err(Timeout)       -> use_last_known()
    Err(NodeGone)      -> deassign(sensor)
    Err(Unreachable)   -> retry_with_backoff()
    Err(Partitioned)   -> enter_readonly_mode()

features.name: Bundled distributed runtime
features.pitch: Cluster membership, Raft consensus and CRDTs are meant to live in every binary as ordinary types, with no Zookeeper, Consul or sidecar.
features.detail: The spec puts the runtime inside every binary as a statically linked library. It holds a scheduler, a network stack, SWIM membership, gossip, failure detection, Raft (`Replicated<T> by quorum N`, which refuses a write without quorum: CP) and CRDT replication through a `Mergeable` capability, whose commutative, associative and idempotent laws are declared like any other law (AP). A node is a region, so a crash takes down its values together. Orphaned remote values are reclaimed by lease. Choosing consistency or availability means choosing a type, so an agent cannot hide the CAP trade-off.
features.status_evidence: None of it exists in the compiler. draconyx-runtime (7.2k lines: codec, image, rt, val) is the native backend's value and call support. It has no networking, membership, consensus, storage drivers or scheduler. `Replicated`, `Sharded` and `ExitReason` are placeholder structs (`raw: Int`) in draconyx-corpus/src/stdlib.rs:436-447. `Mergeable` and `Replicated` exist only as names in the resolver's std inventory (draconyx-resolve/src/std_items.rs:162-163).
features.sample:
capability Mergeable:
    def merge(self: Self, other: Self) -> Self
    law commutative: merge(self = a, other = b) == merge(self = b, other = a)
    law associative: merge(self = merge(self = a, other = b), other = c)
                     == merge(self = a, other = merge(self = b, other = c))
    law idempotent:  merge(self = a, other = a) == a

features.name: Native binaries today; unikernel and Wasm next
features.pitch: `drx build` produces a native executable today, and the spec has the same source compiling to a unikernel that needs no OS underneath, or to a WebAssembly module.
features.detail: Draconyx compiles ahead of time to machine code: no VM, no interpreter and no in-process code generation. The program's meaning lives in one place, so a built binary and `drx run` agree by construction. The spec defines three deployment shapes (hosted binary, unikernel, Wasm module) with one compiler and different runtime components linked per shape. Only the hosted shape is built today.
features.status_evidence: The hosted shape ships. `drx build` (draconyx-cli main.rs:324) uses draconyx-codegen, a Cranelift backend that writes per-package objects and links them with the system `cc` (emit.rs:526). It delegates leaf semantics to draconyx-eval through draconyx-runtime (codegen lib.rs:1-10). That backend still refuses nurseries, `select`, comptime statements, quasi-quotation, placement, kernels, actor sends and remote forms (AX1101-AX1106, emit.rs:437-443). The unikernel and Wasm shapes have no code anywhere in the crates (grep finds nothing for 'unikernel' or 'wasm'). There is no LLVM/MLIR release backend either.

features.name: Hot code swap with checked state migration
features.pitch: Erlang-style hot swap for compiled code: the swap point is proven safe, state is handed over as a linear move, and migrations are functions the compiler checks.
features.detail: A dev host loads a new module version beside the old one, as Erlang does with two versions. Each actor swaps at its message boundary, where the borrow rules prove that no borrow into its state is live. A computed swap-compatibility verdict covers signatures, conformance fingerprints, laws, service requirements and message types. When state layout changes, the host tries each step in order: move, then a typed `migrate` handler, then event-log replay, then supervised restart. For an agent this means edit, swap and observe with state kept warm, within a 250 ms budget.
features.status_evidence: Only the syntax exists. draconyx-parse accepts an actor's `migrate(...) -> State:` block (item.rs:1359-1368), and draconyx-resolve and draconyx-fmt handle it. No crate type-checks or runs `migrate`: draconyx-types, draconyx-own and draconyx-eval have no references to it. There is no `drx dev` command (the CLI verbs are check/fmt/outline/get-def/test/verify/serve/rpc/run/build plus dumps). Actor sends are unsupported in the interpreter (draconyx-eval/src/compile.rs:1023). Nothing loads modules, computes a swap verdict or uses layout hashes for swapping.
features.sample:
actor Accumulator:
    state:
        total: Int
        count: Int

    migrate(transfer old: prev.State) -> State:
        State(total = old.total, count = 0)

    on Add(amount: Int):
        .total = .total + amount
        .count = .count + 1

features.name: Data-race freedom by construction
features.pitch: No Send, no Sync, no annotations: the ownership authorities you already write decide what may cross a task boundary.
features.detail: Sendability is derived from authority, not declared with a marker. A transferred owned value, a readonly borrow or a remote handle may cross; an exclusive borrow or a mutable `share` interior may not. Shared mutable state has to go through a `Mutex`/`RwLock`/atomic bundle. The spec states a Data-Race Freedom theorem for well-typed safe code, so an AI can't write a race that compiles. Today the ownership checker enforces one piece: AX0311 rejects a free-standing `spawn` whose closure captures an exclusive borrow. Bare `share` interiors, channel element types and actor message payloads are not checked yet.
features.status_evidence: draconyx-own/src/check.rs:2826-2840 emits AX0311 NOT_SENDABLE for an exclusive-borrow capture into a free-standing spawn (test crates/draconyx-own/tests/reject/spawn_not_sendable.ax). draconyx-own/src/lib.rs:364-366 lists what is not implemented: sendability of `share` interiors, channels and actor messages. A `Sendable` capability with field-wise derivation and `trust conformance` exists in draconyx-types/src/solve.rs. There is no multithreaded runtime yet: draconyx-eval/src/intrinsics.rs:355 says spawn runs at once in a single-threaded model.

features.name: Structured concurrency with `with nursery`
features.pitch: Tasks can't leak, and child tasks may mutably borrow the parent's data with no locks.
features.detail: A nursery is a `with` target. The block can't exit until every child has finished, a failing child cancels its siblings and the error comes out at block exit, and cancellation is plain scope-exit `Drop`, not an effect or an exception. Because no child outlives the block, children may take exclusive borrows from the enclosing scope, which Rust's `thread::spawn` and Go's goroutines can't offer. For generated code this means no forgotten `join`s and no orphaned goroutines.
features.status_evidence: The parser, formatter and typechecker accept `with nursery` (draconyx-types/src/stmt.rs, draconyx-fmt/src/render.rs). The ownership checker declares the nursery target (draconyx-own/src/check.rs:3806-3811), and AX0311's help suggests `nursery |> spawn(..)` as the fix. Execution is missing: draconyx-eval/src/compile.rs:528 lowers it to "`with nursery` (structured concurrency) is not supported by the v0 interpreter", and the native backend reports it as AX1101 (draconyx-codegen/src/emit.rs:438).
features.sample:
with nursery:
    nursery |> spawn(() -> fetch(transfer url_a))
    nursery |> spawn(() -> fetch(transfer url_b))
    nursery |> spawn(() -> fetch(transfer url_c))
// control does not pass this line until all three children finish

features.name: Move-only channels and a fair, replayable `select`
features.pitch: Every message exists in exactly one place at a time, and `select` timeouts run on a Clock you can fast-forward in tests.
features.detail: Channels are typed sender/receiver pairs. `send` transfers the value, so the producer keeps no alias. `recv` returns ordinary `Err` once the channel is closed and drained, so there is no channel exception. `select` registers on several receivers without consuming anything, picks uniformly at random among ready arms (Go's rule), and consumes only the chosen arm's message. Its `after` timer is driven by the `Clock` service in scope, so tests and replays get deterministic timeouts. Arm-shape rules are compile-time errors.
features.status_evidence: The `select` statement is parsed and typechecked, and its shape rules are enforced: AX1020 SELECT_SHAPE in draconyx-types/src/stmt.rs:575-629, tests crates/draconyx-types/tests/reject/select_shape.ax and select_ok.ax. The interpreter cannot run `select` (draconyx-eval/src/compile.rs:592 marks it unsupported; codegen reports AX1102). std.task spawn/join/channel/send/recv/try_recv run only in a single-threaded interpreter model (draconyx-eval/src/intrinsics.rs:355-361; recv on an empty channel returns Err because no other task can send).
features.sample:
loop:
    select:
        job = recv(borrow work_rx) ->
            match job:
                Ok(j)  -> dispatch(transfer j)
                Err(_) -> break
        _ = recv(borrow shutdown_rx) -> break
        after seconds(30) -> escalate_idle()

features.name: Actors and OTP supervision without exceptions
features.pitch: Erlang-style let-it-crash supervision trees, with errors staying plain Ok/Err data.
features.detail: An actor owns its state exclusively, processes its mailbox one message at a time, and receives messages through the non-blocking `!` operator. Supervisors declare children and an OTP restart strategy (one_for_one, rest_for_one, one_for_all). Crashes reach a supervisor as exit messages, never as thrown values. Restart-to-clean is sound because no peer shares the crashed actor's state. The same parts make up an LLM agent: the actor's state is the transcript, and tools are plain defs. A remote actor (`remote Actor<T>`, fallible `!`) is the language's unit of distribution, and it exists only in the spec.
features.status_evidence: `actor` and `supervisor` declarations are parsed (draconyx-parse/src/item.rs), resolved (draconyx-resolve/src/collect.rs) and typechecked: check_actor/check_supervisor in draconyx-types/src/check.rs:1745-2010 type handler bodies against the state receiver. `spawn_actor` is in the std surface (draconyx-resolve/src/std_items.rs:511). Nothing runs: the actor send `!` is unsupported in the interpreter (draconyx-eval/src/compile.rs:1023) and reported as AX1105 by codegen. There is no mailbox, scheduler, supervisor runtime or remote transport. Actor state across handlers is not ownership-checked (draconyx-own/src/lib.rs:367).
features.sample:
supervisor IngestPipeline:
    strategy: one_for_one
    restart:  transient
    child fetcher: Fetcher = Fetcher()
    child parser:  Parser  = Parser()
    on Crashed(who: ChildId, reason: ExitReason):
        match reason:
            Panicked(_) -> restart(who)
            _           -> escalate(reason)

features.name: Services and dependency injection
features.pitch: Declare a service, `provide` it once in main, and every function underneath can use it. You get no constructor plumbing, no effect rows, and a compile error if a provider is missing.
features.detail: A `service` is an injectable interface called as `Name.op(...)`. `provide` binds it for the rest of a scope, and `provide locally ... in:` swaps it for a single block, which is how a test substitutes a fake without rewriting the code under test. The compiler infers each def's set of required services, so the one static check (AX0501 Missing provider) names the chain of calls that needs the provider. An optional `requires` clause caps that set (AX0502), and per-parameter bounds on higher-order defs are checked at each call (AX0503). For AI-written code, this means the model never threads a logger through twelve signatures, and it can never reach a service nobody configured.
features.status_evidence: Verified end to end today. A scratch package with `provide Greeter = Loud(...)` followed by `provide locally: Greeter = Quiet(...) in:` printed both results under `drx run` (interpreter) and from a `drx build` native binary. Leaving out `provide Console` produced AX0501 with the 'required by main' chain. The codes live in draconyx-types/src/lib.rs:2400-2402 and are emitted at lib.rs:2910/2952/2985, with tests in draconyx-types/tests/types.rs:438-474. One caveat: the check that a provider's value has the service's shape is still only a note ('AX0504 ... not enforced in v0'), which the spec allows (12:77).
features.sample:
def main(transfer system: System) -> Result<Unit>:
    provide Database = postgres.connect(network = system.network, url = DB_URL)
    provide Logger   = new_json_logger(to = system.console)
    serve_requests()

provide locally:
    Database = new_in_memory_database()
    Logger   = NullLogger
in:
    let user = fetch_user(id = UserId(7))

features.name: Object-capability permissions (no ambient authority)
features.pitch: No global `open` and no importable `Network`: the only way code gets authority is to be handed it. Starting from main's `System` powerbox, it can only be narrowed, never widened.
features.detail: Network, FileSystem, Clock, Random, Console, Environment, the GPU and Model are permission values that descend from the single `System` powerbox passed to `main`. They can be attenuated, for example `scope_to(fs, root)`, and a permission is forbidden to embed another permission, so narrowed authority cannot be read back out. That makes generated code safe to run by construction: hand it a filesystem scoped to a scratch directory and it has nothing else. The spec also adds per-dependency permission budgets in the manifest as a supply-chain defense.
features.status_evidence: Works today: the powerbox is minted in draconyx-eval/src/intrinsics.rs:2084. Console and the other services must be provided or you get AX0501 (verified). AX0510 'a permission may not hold a permission' is raised by draconyx-types/src/check.rs:1810 (verified on `strict struct ScopedFs: inner: FileSystem`). `scope_to` reaches the live host filesystem under `drx run`, rooted at the attenuation (intrinsics.rs:3225 n_fs_scope_to; ruling 110). Not built: Network is an inert native, and `scope_to_port` is an identity function (intrinsics.rs:332). Per-dependency permission budgets and `drx add` do not exist, since only path dependencies load and there is no registry. Defect: `def forge() -> FileSystem: FileSystem(live = true)` passes `drx check` with 0 errors. It only traps at run time as 'unresolved name ... not supported', so the spec's statically enforced unforgeability (12:299) is not yet a compile-time check for the std permission services. User `strict` structs are protected (AX0241).
features.sample:
provide locally:
    FileSystem = scope_to(fs = system.filesystem, root = "/tmp/agent-sandbox")
    Network    = new_recording_mock_network()
    Clock      = system.clock
in:
    run_generated_plan()        // cannot touch anything else, by construction

features.name: `tainted`: a typed defense against prompt injection
features.pitch: Model output, console input and the command line are born `tainted`. Passing one to an unmarked parameter, or to a prompt's instruction slot, is compile error AX1022.
features.detail: `tainted T` is a distinct type. A plain T converts into it implicitly, and the only way back is `endorse(value, rationale)`, which demands a stated reason. The std source signatures carry the taint: `Console.read_line`, `System.args`, and `Model` completions. The `Prompt` constructor takes instructions as unmarked `String` and data as `List<tainted String>`, so a program cannot put wire bytes into a model's instruction segment without endorsing them. Its sibling `secret` (AX1023, escaped with `declassify`) stops data from flowing out. This targets the injection path that LLM agents open.
features.status_evidence: The barrier is a single funnel, `Checker::coerce` -> `taint_barrier`, in draconyx-types/src/check.rs:250-300 (rulings 124 and 165). The std signatures are tainted (types.rs test `the_worlds_input_arrives_tainted`, lines 2318-2340). Verified with `drx check`: passing a tainted String to a String parameter gives AX1022, `std.ai.prompt(instruction = t, ...)` gives AX1022, and propagation through `t ++ "x"` gives AX1022. Hole: string interpolation launders taint. `let u = "hello {t}"` passed to a String parameter produces no diagnostic, which contradicts 12:472 ('an interpolated string with one tainted segment included'). features.name: `trust` blocks: unsafe code that names its reason
features.pitch: Draconyx has no `unsafe`. It has `trust "why this holds":`, where every unchecked call site carries a mandatory written rationale an auditor can grep.
features.detail: Code the compiler cannot verify is marked by its epistemic status, using the same `trust` keyword that marks unverified laws. A `trust` block admits exactly seven enumerated powers. Calling a `trust def` outside a block is an error (AX0801), and a trust construct without its rationale string is a parse error (AX0269), so every vouched call site states its obligation in prose. The spec pairs this with FFI to C/C++ in three per-library modes (sandboxed in Wasm by default, isolated, in_process) and with Wasm in both directions. Extern calls outside trust are typed `Result<T, Trapped>`.
features.status_evidence: The static trust tier ships. AX0801 is emitted in draconyx-types/src/call.rs:1065 and tested at types.rs:514 and selfhost/units4/68-trust-tier, which covers nested blocks, lambdas, pipelines and witness families. The mandatory rationale is AX0269. `extern "C" def ... from library` declarations type-check with the sandboxed `Result<T, Trapped>` proxy (units4/55-extern-modes). Not built: actually calling foreign code. `drx run` on `extern "C" def abs(x: Int) -> Int from library "c"` exits 2 with '`ffi.main.abs` has no body'. No crate depends on libloading, dlopen, wasmtime or wasmer, and the [native] modes, the Wasm sandbox and Wasm export are spec-only.

features.name: With blocks: one keyword for receiver, destructuring and scoped release
features.pitch: One `with` covers Python's context managers, Rust's RAII and multi-value destructuring, even at the end of a pipeline.
features.detail: A `with` block fixes a target in a scope and exposes its parts under bare names: `.field` against an implicit receiver, a destructured tuple from a multi-return call, or an owned `Drop` value released when the scope is done. An agent gets one uniform construct to generate where other languages need three idioms. A `|> with (mean, sd):` stage destructures the result of a pipeline without tuple-splatting.
features.status_evidence: draconyx-parse parses all forms (Stmt::With, Expr::WithStage). draconyx-eval/src/compile.rs:507-535 lowers the implicit-receiver and destructuring forms, and :1832 lowers the piped `|> with` stage. draconyx-eval/src/interp.rs:727 runs them, and draconyx-codegen/src/lower.rs handles St::With natively. Drop runs in reverse declaration order under ruling 158 (interp.rs:1430), but the release happens at frame exit under refcount ownership, so 'released exactly at the block's end' was not verified. Two forms are unsupported and return AX1101/AX1103: `with nursery` (concurrency) and a bare `with` stage outside a pipeline.

features.name: Shapes and named axes in the type
features.pitch: A tensor's dtype, axis names and sizes belong to its type, so a mismatched matmul is meant to fail at compile time, before any array is allocated.
features.detail: `Tensor<F32; batch: B, feature: D>` puts named axes and size variables into the type. matmul's contract becomes a type equation over the shared inner size, and a transposed argument becomes a type error rather than silently wrong numbers, which is the classic bug in AI-written numerical code. Library signatures bind axis names generically while user signatures keep them literal, so a shared library still catches a caller's transpose mistakes.

In draconyx-types/src/unify.rs (TENSOR_FQN), a Tensor written with no axis segment unifies with every `Tensor<dt; ...>`. draconyx-types/src/lib.rs:280 says 'Tensor axis segments stay opaque text' and lists 'tensor named-axis algebra (opaque by text)' under Not implemented. Axis segments are parsed, carried as `cuts` (decision 222) and hashed, but the spec's compile error for a shape mismatch is not emitted today. Mixing dtypes (F32 vs I8, quantize/dequantize) is caught.

features.name: grad, vmap, jit as typed function transforms, with schedules certified by laws
features.pitch: Autodiff, auto-batching and fusion are plain functions over functions, and schedule rewrites are gated by laws instead of being trusted.
features.detail: Following JAX, `grad`, `jvp`, `vmap`, `pmap` and `jit` each take a function and return a function. They compose by ordinary application (`grad(grad(loss))`, `jit(grad(f))`), and a path through a non-differentiable operation is a compile error. Following Halide, a schedule (`@tile`, `@fuse`, `@vectorize`, `@on`) is a separate block from the algorithm. The spec's addition is that a directive compiles only if the laws it relies on hold at the build's verification level, while XLA, TVM and Halide trust their transformations.
features.status_evidence: compiler/std/src/tensor.ax:207-260 declares grad, jvp, vjp, jacfwd, jacrev, jit, compile and with_precision as signatures with no bodies. vmap and pmap forward to a `trust def vmap_raw` that has no implementation. Because the signatures exist, calls to them type-check, but nothing differentiates, batches or fuses, and draconyx-eval has no tensor intrinsics. draconyx-parse/src/item.rs:215 parses `schedule` blocks, and draconyx-resolve/src/lib.rs:94-97 treats schedule directives as opaque. Law gating of directives is not implemented.

features.name: Hygienic, typed dialects (macros, elab, comptime)
features.pitch: Dialects extend the syntax with Racket-grade hygiene and type-directed elaboration, without textual macros.
features.detail: Extensions use Racket's set-of-scopes hygiene, so identifiers a dialect generates cannot capture the user's identifiers, and deliberate capture goes through syntax parameters. There are two type-blind tiers (declarative `pattern => template`, and `lower`) and two typed hooks (`elab` synthesizes code from the expected type, `typecheck` can only veto), all written in `comptime` Draconyx. Generated code keeps source provenance, so diagnostics point at what the agent actually wrote.
features.status_evidence: The surface is parsed: draconyx-parse handles comptime `emit:` quasi-quotes and `require`. draconyx-resolve/src/lib.rs:924 checks the `use extension` activation DAG for cycles (a resolver check), and draconyx-resolve/src/lib.rs:94-97 resolves comptime bodies leniently and treats macro patterns and quasi-quotes as opaque. No macro expansion or hygiene engine exists. draconyx-types/src/check.rs:1757 skips extensions with COMPTIME_SKIPPED, draconyx-eval/src/compile.rs:601 reports 'comptime statements are not supported by the v0 interpreter', and codegen refuses them as AX1103/AX1104. rows.label: Named arguments required at every multi-argument call of a declared function
rows.judging_rule: yes = the compiler rejects an unlabelled argument at every call of a declared function with 2+ parameters, and the author has no opt-out. part = labels are required by default but the author can opt out (Swift `_`), or the author can opt in (Python keyword-only `*`). no = TS, Java, C#, C++, Rust, Go, Zig, Elixir, Mojo, where named args are optional or don't exist.

rows.label: Mutation and moves spelled at the call site
rows.judging_rule: yes = both mutation and ownership transfer must be written at every call site, receivers included. part = only one is marked, or only some calls (Rust `&mut` but moves and method auto-borrow unmarked; Swift `&` for inout plus optional `consume`; C# `ref`/`out` but mutation through references unmarked; Mojo `^` for transfer but mutation unmarked). no = Python, TS, Java, C++, Go, Zig, Elixir.

rows.label: Missing and redundant match arms both rejected, on every match
rows.judging_rule: yes = on every match/switch over a closed type, both a missing case and an unreachable/redundant case are compile ERRORS. part = exhaustiveness is enforced but redundancy is only a warning, or the check covers only some match forms (Rust and Swift warn on unreachable patterns; Java checks pattern/expression switches but not legacy statement switches; TS needs a `never` idiom; C# warns on non-exhaustive). Zig is yes on enum/union switch (missing prong error, duplicate prong error, unreachable else error). no = Python, Go, Elixir, C++ (warnings only), Mojo (no match).

rows.label: Deterministic agent protocol: same source tree, byte-identical answers
rows.judging_rule: yes = the compiler ships a query protocol for agents whose answers are specified to be byte-identical for the same source tree. An LSP server does not count. All eleven others: no.

rows.label: Ownership and borrows checked at compile time, with no tracing garbage collector and no lifetime annotations
rows.judging_rule: yes = use-after-move and aliasing of mutable borrows are rejected statically, the runtime has no tracing GC, AND the language has no lifetime/origin annotation syntax. part = two of the three (Rust: static and no GC, but lifetime syntax; Swift: ARC and no lifetimes, but exclusivity is partly a run-time trap and copies are implicit; Mojo: static ownership and ASAP destruction, but origin parameters). no = Python, TS, Java, C#, Go, Elixir (tracing GC), C++ and Zig (no static check). rows.label: Generic code dispatches on the algebraic laws a type satisfies, with arm totality checked

C++ concepts, Rust traits, Swift protocols, Java/C# interfaces and Go constraints are signature-only: no. All eleven others: no.

rows.label: Remote values in the type: partial failure typed, remote references can't be shared, distributed runtime bundled

rows.label: Structured concurrency (nurseries) with data races rejected at compile time
